project: Wuxia Life P65 Merchant Trilogy Player Experience Reconciliation
description: Audit the current apprentice, tavern, and peasant merchant trilogy as one player-facing package, then rank whether success-cost differentiation, success-shape differentiation, or recap-line strength is the thinnest layer before opening the next bounded optimization stage.

userStories.title: Audit merchant trilogy as a player route package
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want one player-route audit across P58, P59, P61, P63, and P64 so the repo has a single truth source for what the merchant trilogy currently feels like end-to-end.
acceptanceCriteria: Summarize player-visible differences across bridge, entry, pressure, and payoff for apprentice, tavern, and peasant merchant routes
Separate strong existing differentiation from layers that may still feel structurally similar to players
Save docs/test-reports/p65-merchant-trilogy-player-route-audit.md
Do not change runtime behavior in this story
userStories.notes: Audit complete. Strong differentiation at bridge and entry layers; thinning at pressure, payoff, and ending layers. No runtime changes.

userStories.title: Lock P65 experience-reconciliation scope contract
userStories.description: As a planner, I want a scope contract so P65 stays a player-experience reconciliation stage instead of quietly turning into another merchant content expansion.
acceptanceCriteria: Limit P65 to player-experience reconciliation, comparison, and priority sorting
Define allowed layers: documentation comparison and only the minimum validation reinforcement if needed
List forbidden expansions: new merchant content wave, new systems, and new ordinary-to-mixed route implementation
Save docs/test-reports/p65-merchant-trilogy-experience-scope-contract.md
userStories.notes: Scope contract complete. P65 locked as reconciliation/comparison/priority-sorting stage with zero default runtime changes.

userStories.title: Evaluate success-cost differentiation
userStories.description: As a designer, I want an explicit assessment of whether the three merchant routes already feel like they pay different prices for success.
acceptanceCriteria: Compare apprentice, tavern, and peasant success-cost signals using the existing runtime-visible route package
State whether the three costs already feel like different chosen lives rather than one merchant burden with light variation
If the layer is weak, identify which route and which route phase is thinnest
Write the conclusion into the P65 reconciliation artifact
userStories.notes: Evaluation complete. Moderate differentiation — cost is described (expression layer) but not felt (structural layer). Thinnest: peasant route at payoff phase. Written to reconciliation doc §2.

userStories.title: Evaluate success-shape differentiation
userStories.description: As a designer, I want an explicit assessment of whether the three merchant routes already feel like they succeed in different ways.
acceptanceCriteria: Compare the player-facing sense of what each route relies on to grow successful
State whether the differences are strong enough to support distinct success shapes
If the layer is weak, identify whether the missing force sits at entry, pressure, or payoff
Write the conclusion into the P65 reconciliation artifact
userStories.notes: Evaluation complete. Moderate-weak differentiation — success is flavored but not shaped. Missing force at payoff layer. Written to reconciliation doc §3.

userStories.title: Evaluate recap-line and destiny-sentence strength
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to know whether the current trilogy already gives players a clear sentence they can use to summarize what kind of merchant life they lived.
acceptanceCriteria: Assess the current recall strength of player-summary lines across all three merchant routes
State whether each route already supports a clear and distinct destiny sentence
If the layer is weak, identify which route lacks enough closing force
Do not require a new recap or ending system in this story
userStories.notes: Evaluation complete. Moderate mid-journey, weak at ending. No distinct destiny sentence at final gate. Weakest: peasant route. Written to reconciliation doc §4.

userStories.title: Rank the three experience layers
userStories.description: As a planner, I want P65 to rank success-cost differentiation, success-shape differentiation, and recap-line strength so the next merchant stage optimizes the highest-value pain first.
acceptanceCriteria: Rank success-cost differentiation, success-shape differentiation, and recap-line strength in priority order
Bind the ranking to repo-grounded runtime truth rather than generic product judgment
Choose one unique next-cut optimization target for P66
Record the ranking and recommendation in closure or appendix
userStories.notes: Ranking complete. Priority: (1) success-cost differentiation → (2) recap-line strength → (3) success-shape differentiation. P66 target: success-cost differentiation. Written to reconciliation doc §5.

userStories.title: Add narrow validation reinforcement if needed
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want only the minimum additional validation needed to support the experience-priority conclusion, without reopening the merchant trilogy implementation.
acceptanceCriteria: If existing proof and tests are sufficient, record that no additional validation is needed
If existing evidence is insufficient, add only the smallest comparison-level validation asset needed to support the ranking
Do not rewrite the P58, P59, P61, P63, or P64 test systems
Relevant commands pass
userStories.notes: No additional validation needed. Existing test coverage is sufficient: P58/P59/P61 bridge tests (14-18 assertions each), P63 entry differentiation tests (4 test functions), P64 pressure/payoff differentiation tests (1 test function). All tests pass. Typecheck passes. Priority ranking conclusion is well-supported by existing repo-grounded evidence.

userStories.title: Produce P65 closure report
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want a closure report stating which player-experience layer is now the top optimization priority for the merchant trilogy and why.
acceptanceCriteria: Save docs/test-reports/p65-merchant-trilogy-player-experience-closure-report.md
Summarize the route audit, the three layer evaluations, the priority ranking, and the next-stage recommendation
State the boundary between P65 and the planned P66 and P67 stages
List larger playtest, new-route, or system-level work that remains deferred
userStories.notes: Closure report complete. Top priority: success-cost differentiation (P66 target). All 8 stories pass.
